instruction.text: Select the image of a Viking ship.

atoms.b: This is a Viking longship that was built for raiding. These ships were ((++fast slow)), light and easy to move.
Vikings also used slower, smaller passenger and cargo ships called knarrs. These ships were ((++strong weak)) and sturdy and could hold lots of cargo.

instruction.text: Find the features of this Viking longship.

feedback.end: Each Viking ship had a large, brightly-coloured sail that helped them to move in the water.
When there wasn’t enough wind to use the sail, the men used to row with long, wooden oars.
Hand painted Viking shields were attached to the side of the ship for defence.
At the front of the ship, there was a carved, wooden figurehead of a creature like a dragon or snake. This was was designed to scare people.

instruction.text: Vikings didn’t use maps to navigate. What do you think they used instead?

feedback.end: They also used landmarks on the shore to guide them.

atoms.b: The Vikings travelled and traded all over the ((++world Solar_System)). Some daring explorers even travelled across the Atlantic Ocean to North America!
Leif Erikson made it all the way to Newfoundland in modern-day Canada. We know this because archaeologists have found the remains of a ((++Viking Roman)) settlement there.

instruction.text: Build the picture of a Viking coin.

feedback.end: Archaeologists have found coins like this buried in Viking hoards. Some hoards even included coins from Arabic countries, like Syria and Iraq, which shows the Vikings likely travelled to these countries too!

instruction.text: Which two things do you think the Vikings traded?

feedback.end: The Vikings traded things like amber, ivory and animal fur. In return, they received things like gold, silver, silk and fine pottery. They would also capture and enslave people on their raids and sell them in other countries.
